question: How does anion ordering affect valence band maximum positions and photocatalytic performance in CaTaO₂N?
answer: Anion ordering in CaTaO₂N significantly affects valence band maximum (VBM) positions and photocatalytic performance by altering orbital interactions and electronic structure. Three-dimensional (3D) anion ordering motifs stabilize the VBM through stronger Ta 5d–N 2p orbital overlap, lowering VBM positions by up to 0.5 eV compared to 2D motifs. This stabilization enhances photocatalytic oxygen evolution by positioning the VBM closer to the water oxidation potential. Additionally, 3D ordering increases hole effective mass anisotropy, reducing hole mobility but extending carrier lifetimes due to fewer relaxation pathways. The covalent Ta-N interactions in 3D motifs, evidenced by shorter bond lengths and larger bond angle asymmetry, further contribute to VBM stabilization. These findings demonstrate that 3D anion ordering optimizes CaTaO₂N for oxygen evolution by tuning electronic structure and carrier dynamics.

The purpose of the paper is to investigate how different anion ordering arrangements in CaTaO₂N influence its electronic structure and photocatalytic properties. Specifically, the study explores the effects of anion ordering on the valence band structure, bandgaps, carrier effective masses, and band edge positions, with an emphasis on their implications for photocatalytic oxygen evolution. The findings highlight the role of orbital overlap between Ta 5d and N 2p bands in determining the electronic properties of the material.
